label: prf:figure-eight-branching-rule
title: Proof of figure eight branching rule
html:
Proof. The figure-eight braid 4_1 lives in H_3(R, q) (three strands). Its character in an irreducible representation \rho_\lambda of H_k(R, q) with k \geq 3 factors through the restriction H_k(R, q) \downarrow H_3(R, q):

  \chi(4_1, \lambda)
  = \sum_{\mu \,\vdash\, 3} f^{\lambda/\mu} \cdot \chi(4_1, \mu)

where f^{\lambda/\mu} is the branching multiplicity --- the number of standard Young tableaux of skew shape \lambda/\mu, counting the distinct ways to remove k - 3 cells from \lambda along a saturated chain in Young's lattice to arrive at \mu.

The three partitions of 3 contribute:

See Table 1.

Substituting:

  \chi(4_1, \lambda)
  = f^{\lambda/[3]} \cdot 1
  + f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} \cdot (-1 - h^2)
  + f^{\lambda/[1^3]} \cdot 1

Collecting the constant and h^2 terms gives the result.

Combinatorial structure of b_\lambda. Since b_\lambda = -f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} is always non-positive, and f^{\lambda/[2{,}1]} = 0 if and only if \lambda does not contain the Young diagram of [2{,}1] (i.e.\ \lambda is a single row [k] or a single column [1^k]), the q-deformation correction vanishes precisely for the trivial and sign representations.

For the dominant partitions at each level:

See Table 2.

The BW scaling of each partition is determined by:

  1. Content sum c(\lambda) = \sum_{(i,j) \in \lambda} (j - i): positive \to A-dominated (volume/surface), negative \to Z/N-dominated (Coulomb/exchange), zero \to isospin-sensitive (Wigner/hook).

  2. Self-conjugacy (\lambda = \lambda'): self-conjugate partitions contribute isospin Casimir terms (T(T+1)/A, T(T+1)(T+2)/A^2, etc.).

  3. Conjugate pairing (\{\lambda, \lambda'\} with \lambda \neq \lambda'): the sum \lambda \oplus \lambda' gives charge-symmetric corrections (form factor, pn correlation).

  4. Hook partitions ([k-r, 1^r]): the H_3 \hookrightarrow H_k branching multiplicity determines shell effects via the nuclear magic numbers. \square
